video_title: Jaylen Brown Opens Up on How NBA Wealth Changed His Life & Relationships

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the pressure of being raised by a single mother
quotes.excerpt: I was raised by a single mom, so I just wanted to alleviate any pressure I could on my side.
quotes.quote: I was raised by a single mom, so I just wanted to alleviate any pressure I could on my side.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the emotional toll of sudden wealth and envy
quotes.excerpt: I had to learn to deal with envy. It changes you. Conversations become invoices. Lines get blurred.
quotes.quote: Friends, family, they can let you down. I had to learn to deal with envy. It changes you. Conversations become invoices. Lines get blurred. But that's been the hardest part for me to navigate, because it puts you on an island, isolates you.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on finding true wealth beyond money
quotes.excerpt: Money don't make you rich, baby. I'm rich in life, I'm rich in experience, I'm rich in adversity.
quotes.quote: Money don't make you rich, baby. I'm rich in life, I'm rich in experience, I'm rich in adversity. I'm rich in prosperity. That makes me happy. You got to develop tools of discernment, but only experience can kind of give you that.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on his early experiences with financial inequality
quotes.excerpt: I had friends who had things that I didn't have. I think that was my earliest experience.
quotes.quote: I was raised by a single mom, so our resources were limited to some degree. Even though my mom had a really good job, at times there was recessions in Atlanta. She had to work multiple jobs just to make sure she could provide. So, I had friends who had things that I didn't have. I think that was my earliest experience where you could just tell they had the newest gear or shoes, and we couldn't afford to get that. So I guess some of my earliest memories would be around seeing kind of when others around me, families have more and we had less.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on how basketball changed his family's financial situation
quotes.excerpt: As basketball came into the picture, things shifted. My platform and my level of play demanded attention.
quotes.quote: As basketball came into the picture, things shifted. My platform and my level of play demanded attention that wasn't necessarily monetary wealth, but you could see wealth was being accumulated. I didn't have to pay for camps anymore, or my mom didn't have to pay for camps anymore. At around 13 or 14 years old, I didn't have to pay for basketball sneakers anymore. Anything basketball-related, traveling or going to tournaments, I had to pay for like just your normal everyday expenses, food or travel or hotel, but for the most part, everything from then had been covered. So as basketball came into the picture, it also brought value in a different way that kind of shifted that dynamic at a very early age.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on living like a college student despite NBA wealth
quotes.excerpt: The first three years of my career, I still lived like I was in college.
quotes.quote: The first three years of my career, I still lived like I was in college. I ate, I didn't have a chef, I ate like the same type of foods, I Ubered, I didn't have a car. But when I would go out and buy like some nice car, I kind of just operated like I was still in college. For the first three years, my idea of money didn't really settle in yet.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on prioritizing community investment over personal spending
quotes.excerpt: How can I invest in my community first and then figure out how I can make monetary value.
quotes.quote: Community is one. I know a lot of people look at like, I'm going to make as much money then I'm going to give back 10% or something like that. I flip it. How can I invest in my community first and then figure out how I can make monetary value in a different way. I'm always looking about doing projects that align with myself, but also align with my community that solve problems or create solutions.

As a young person developing that, either a three-month window or six-month window before you start to evaluate things, are they going, how much money was spent, then you can make a decision from there.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the pressure of early fame and success
quotes.excerpt: As a 15, 16-year-old, you could already start to see my projection because I was a highly ranked.
quotes.quote: As a 15, 16-year-old, you could already start to see my projection because I was a highly ranked, highly touted, you know, I was being talked about, I was on TV at an early age. But I also come from the same backgrounds that a lot of my peers around me came from, single-parent household, lack of resources, lack of opportunity, but they're seeing me start to separate myself. Naturally, I had to learn to deal with envy. I've had a immense amount of luck and favor from the creator to help me get to where I am.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the necessity of stoicism in managing relationships
quotes.excerpt: I think stoicism is something that I had to develop where it's like no emotion.
quotes.quote: I think stoicism is something that I had to develop where it's like no emotion, but it's like you're just the same every single day. Because, you know, friends, family, they can let you down, man. They can, they can disappoint you in ways that, it changes you. And the amount of money, the amount of clout, the amount of fame that you're able to acquire puts pressure on the people around you, especially the ones closest to you. And sometimes that can cause damage to relationships, unintentionally, just by you just being successful or you just trying to help your community or you just trying to be the best version you could possibly be for your family.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on his gratitude and commitment to future generations
quotes.excerpt: God has already provided me with more than I could ever ever imagine.
quotes.quote: God has already provided me with more than I could ever ever imagine. If I never make another dollar in this lifetime again, I'm extremely grateful for everything that I have. So, for me, my approach is everything that I gain from this moment on or in the future will be with the intent to invest back into my community or invest back into the next generation. So, I'll have everything that I could have imagined, and I'm extremely grateful for that.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of financial oversight for young athletes
quotes.excerpt: Keep an eye on your money from day one. Be careful who you give approvals to.
quotes.quote: Keep an eye on your money from day one. You know what I mean? Attractions, be careful who you give approvals to from advisors. Like even if you get busy or people are encouraging you to do things, be like, it'll be all right, they can wait. You know, make sure that you can have a level eye on what's going on with your money. It's extremely helpful in terms of like being able to create the life that you want and finding peace. I think money definitely can help bring you that, that peace of mind that you're looking for.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the necessity of multiple approvals for financial decisions

quotes.quote: I give a, I refer like there should be three approvals before anything gets done. Just so there's a level of order that takes place, because you get busy and you look at things and you might only seen it once and people approve stuff and then it's bills that pile up and you wonder where they came from. I would say just try to keep an eye on it as best you can.
